name: Michal
description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David arose with his men, slew two hundred Philistines, and brought their foreskins in full tale to the king; he doubled the order. That is how devoted a warrior he was for his king and his nation, and Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

points: Saul sent messengers unto David's house to watch him and to slay him in the morning. Having tried to turn his son against David, he now leans on his daughter, David's own wife; but Michal warned David, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.
At this time Michal was a righteous example, a ride or die; she was a tower against death to her husband. She turns sour some chapters down the line, but here she saved his life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: Michal let David down through a window, and he fled and escaped; she laid an image in the bed with a pillow of goats' hair for his bolster and said, He is sick. Saul said, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him, and found the image; Michal covered herself, saying David threatened her, but she was looking out for her husband.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they were also both of them his wives; but Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: Abner sent messengers to David offering to bring all Israel to him. David agreed to make a league, but required that Michal, Saul's daughter, first be brought to him, and he sent to Ishbosheth to deliver his wife whom he had espoused for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal the daughter of Saul looked out the window and despised David in her heart as he danced and played. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites
